raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MoE inference normally places attention and routed experts on the same GPU group. This PR adds Attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD), allowing them to run on separate groups. Multiple attention instances can share one FFN instance and its routed-expert weights, so attention capacity can grow without replicating those weights for every instance.

Requests continue to use SGLang's serving APIs on the attention instances. AFD is opt-in through `--afd-role`.

![SGLang AFD: tokens from multiple attention instances form shared expert batches, and Megamoe M2N overlaps attention with remote expert execution across microbatches and layers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd4e8f84-4272-4fee-a4a4-3b7e7df6d54c)

F batches routed tokens across A instances. In the Megamoe M2N decode path, per-microbatch communication lanes overlap with attention computation, while one persistent kernel per F rank processes successive layers and microbatches. Timing in the diagram is schematic.

## Modifications

- Add attention (A) and FFN (F) roles, startup handshakes, role-specific weight loading, and remote expert execution. A owns requests, KV cache, attention, routing, shared experts, and sampling; F owns routed experts.
- Support asymmetric A/F parallelism, CUDA graphs, decode microbatch overlap, and batching across attention instances sharing F. F graph and dispatch capacities are derived from the attention handshakes.
- Provide staged NCCL and NVSHMEM transports, Direct DeepEP, and Megamoe M2N. NCCL uses standard SGLang dependencies; other backends load their optional components only when selected.
- Integrate Qwen3 MoE, Qwen3.5 MoE, DeepSeek V3/V3.2/V4, and the GLM-5 MoE DSA family, including EAGLE/MTP and DSpark with draft execution on A.
- Add coverage to the registered CPU test suites, an AFD deployment guide, and a DeepSeek-V4-Pro Megamoe M2N recipe.

### Usage and scope

Start attention workers with `--afd-role attn --afd-ffn-addr <ffn-host>:<port>` and FFN workers with `--afd-role ffn`. For a shared F, set `--afd-attn-instances` to the number of attention instances. Send generation requests to A.

Complete deployment examples and the backend/precision support matrix are in `docs/docs/advanced_features/afd_disaggregation.mdx`. The multi-host Pro recipe is in `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx`.

The initial implementation uses fixed membership established at startup and homogeneous attention instances, with TP size one within each attention DP group. Direct backends require pure expert parallelism on F. Direct MegaMoE requires SM100/SM103 GPUs with peer-accessible memory; cross-host execution requires a shared NVLink fabric with CUDA FABRIC access. The deployment guide lists the remaining feature combinations and restrictions.

<details>
<summary>Optional components</summary>

Install the component required by the selected backend on all participating workers.

| Backend | Package / required API | Public source and release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nccl` | Standard SGLang dependencies | No additional AFD component |
| `nvshmem` | `afd-nvshmem` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/afd-nvshmem/tree/15a7764608f8211e6a564270608fb53e23e5a591) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/afd-nvshmem/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261019) |
| `direct_deepep` | `sgl-deep-ep` exposing `deep_ep.afd` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepEP/tree/dcd018ba3e1a6d4f892eb9cd8a10e73dfb8bb54d) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepEP/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261019) |
| `direct_megamoe` | `sgl-deep-gemm` exposing `deep_gemm.mega.m2n` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/tree/991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261028) |

The AFD DeepEP build also provides the standard DeepEP APIs. The required AFD extensions are not yet included in the official component wheels.

Related component PRs: [DeepEP #14](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepEP/pull/14) (target `sgl-deepep`) and [DeepGEMM #110](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/110) (target `dev`).

The M2N component adapts code from [FastAFD](https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/FastAFD/tree/3c7161949310b6d59d6b4cf9bf997a4935c8113b). Source attribution and original copyright/license notices are retained in the component repository and package.

</details>

## Accuracy Tests

For each model, we compare colocated inference and AFD using identical evaluation prompts, checkpoints, quantization, and sampling parameters. Source revisions and evaluation settings are listed below. Speculative decoding uses actual acceptance without simulation.

| GPU architecture | Model | Benchmark | Colocate (%) | AFD (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| SM103 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | GSM8K | 94.84 | 95.07 |
| SM103 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | GPQA Diamond | 87.12 ± 1.20 | 86.74 ± 2.04 |
| SM100 | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GSM8K | 95.91 | 96.51 |
| SM100 | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GPQA Diamond | 69.44 ± 0.87 | 69.82 ± 1.51 |
| SM103 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | GSM8K | 97.12 | 97.57 |
| SM103 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | GPQA Diamond | 88.01 ± 1.95 | 88.51 ± 0.76 |
| SM100 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 | GSM8K | 90.90 | 90.90 |
| SM100 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 | GPQA Diamond | 87.12 ± 0.65 | 88.38 ± 1.24 |

- GSM8K: all 1,319 test questions, 0-shot, one run with seed 0.
- GPQA Diamond: all 198 questions, 0-shot, `--n-repeats 4`, without a fixed seed. Results are mean accuracy ± standard deviation across the four repetitions.
- Evaluation concurrency: 256. Evaluator: `sgl-eval==0.1.2`.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation parameters</summary>

| Parameter | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reasoning mode | Thinking, `reasoning_effort=high` | `enable_thinking=true` | `enable_thinking=true` | `enable_thinking=true` |
| Temperature | 1.0 | 0.6 | 1.0 | 0.6 |
| `top_p` | 1.0 | 0.95 | 0.95 | 0.95 |
| `top_k` | Unrestricted | 20 | Unrestricted | 20 |
| `min_p` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Maximum output tokens, including reasoning | 65,536 | 30,000 | 65,536 | 32,768 |

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Decode-only

ShareGPT prompts with 8,192 input tokens, a 90% shared prefix, and 512 output tokens.

For the SM100/SM103 results below, we compare colocated EP8/attention-DP8 using DeepEP with AFD attention TP4/attention-DP4 instances sharing EP8 FFN workers. Both use attention TP1 per DP rank. AFD decode uses Megamoe M2N; F uses DeepEP for staged prefill. Throughput per GPU includes every GPU in the deployment, including A and F. Each marker below is a measured configuration; lines connect the selected points as visual guides.

The DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3-235B, and GLM-5.2 results predate the [M2N memory-access optimization](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/commit/991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c) and retain their original measurements and source revisions. The Qwen3.5 results use this optimization. Separate measurements showed up to **3.3% higher decode throughput** from the optimization in the tested configurations.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED PERFORMANCE SUMMARY -->

Selected comparisons at similar TPOT (colocate → AFD):

- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 1.52× throughput/GPU**, at 10.32 → 10.22 ms.
- **Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8: 2.68× throughput/GPU**, at 14.36 → 14.30 ms.
- **GLM-5.2-NVFP4: 1.78× throughput/GPU**, at 6.87 → 6.85 ms.
- **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8: 2.67× throughput/GPU**, at 17.33 → 17.32 ms.

<!-- END GENERATED PERFORMANCE SUMMARY -->

![Decode throughput per GPU versus TPOT for DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, and GLM-5.2-NVFP4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/710d6285-4971-4e31-9f91-7cda724f59f4)

<details>

The Qwen3.5 accuracy and performance results cover text workloads and use the Qwen3.5/AFD implementation corresponding to SGLang `932ba87c338f31888c4da8e823112ad67b0aa2fc` and DeepGEMM `991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c`.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""Measure fixed-batch decode throughput with SGLang's streaming API.

Requires Python 3.11+. Dependencies:
    pip install aiohttp transformers huggingface_hub orjson
    pip install datasets  # Only needed to download GSM8K.

Example:
    python bench_decode.py --model /path/to/model --concurrency 256 \
        --base-url 127.0.0.1:30000 --input-len 8192 --prefix-len 7373

The default dataset is ShareGPT. --dataset gsm8k uses openai/gsm8k, configuration
main, split train. Both download through the Hugging Face cache unless a local
JSON/JSONL --dataset-path is given. Prompts use ShareGPT's first conversation turn
or GSM8K's question field, without a chat template. Explicit input lengths
repeat/truncate token IDs; the shared prefix is part of that length.

All requests must fit concurrently, and all prefill must finish before decode
starts. All URLs must share one coordinated decode schedule.

Record the total received token count when every request has returned tokens,
then again when the first request finishes. Throughput is the count difference
divided by the elapsed client time. Counts come directly from streaming metadata,
without interpolation. HTTP delivery order can shift the boundaries relative to
GPU steps; this is client-observed throughput, not exact GPU timing.
TPOT is concurrency / throughput, expressed in milliseconds for this window.
Streaming updates are buffered every 8 tokens by default to avoid output-path
backlog at high concurrency. Counts still come from cumulative metadata; no
interpolation is used. --stream-interval 1 requests per-token updates.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import random
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import aiohttp
import orjson

SHAREGPT_REPO = "anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered"
SHAREGPT_FILE = "ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json"


def resize_tokens(tokens: list[int], length: int) -> list[int]:
    return (tokens * ((length + len(tokens) - 1) // len(tokens)))[:length]


def load_dataset_rows(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[dict]:
    if args.dataset == "gsm8k" and not args.dataset_path:
        from datasets import load_dataset

        return list(load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="train"))

    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

    dataset_path = args.dataset_path or hf_hub_download(
        repo_id=SHAREGPT_REPO, filename=SHAREGPT_FILE, repo_type="dataset"
    )
    with open(dataset_path) as f:
        if dataset_path.endswith(".jsonl"):
            return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
        return json.load(f)


def load_prompts(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[list[int]]:
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    dataset = load_dataset_rows(args)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
    random.Random(args.seed).shuffle(dataset)

    prompts = []
    prefix = []
    for row in dataset:
        if args.dataset == "gsm8k":
            text = row["question"]
        else:
            conversation = row.get("conversations", row.get("conversation", []))
            if len(conversation) < 2:
                continue
            text = conversation[0]["value"]
        tokens = tokenizer.encode(text)
        if len(tokens) < 2:
            continue
        if args.prefix_len and not prefix:
            prefix = resize_tokens(tokens, args.prefix_len)
            continue
        if args.input_len is not None:
            tokens = resize_tokens(tokens, args.input_len - args.prefix_len)
        prompts.append(prefix + tokens)
        if len(prompts) == args.concurrency:
            return prompts
    raise ValueError(f"Dataset has only {len(prompts)} usable prompts")


@dataclass
class DecodeCounter:
    counts: list[int]
    output_len: int
    finished: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    num_started: int = 0
    total_tokens: int = 0
    all_started: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
    start: tuple[float, int] | None = None
    end: tuple[float, int] | None = None

    def record(self, index: int, meta: dict, now: float) -> None:
        count = meta["completion_tokens"]
        previous = self.counts[index]
        if index in self.finished or not previous <= count <= self.output_len:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid token progress: {previous} -> {count}")
        self.total_tokens += count - previous
        self.counts[index] = count
        if previous == 0 and count > 0:
            self.num_started += 1
            if self.num_started == len(self.counts):
                self.start = (now, self.total_tokens)
                self.all_started.set()
        reason = meta["finish_reason"]
        if reason is not None:
            if reason["type"] != "length" or count != self.output_len:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Incomplete generation: {count} tokens, {reason}")
            self.finished.add(index)
            if self.end is None:
                self.end = (now, self.total_tokens)

    def result(self) -> dict:
        if (
            len(self.finished) != len(self.counts)
            or self.start is None
            or self.end is None
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Every request must produce tokens and finish successfully"
            )
        start_time, start_tokens = self.start
        end_time, end_tokens = self.end
        if end_time <= start_time or end_tokens <= start_tokens:
            raise ValueError(
                "No common decode window: a request finished before all started"
            )
        duration = end_time - start_time
        measured_tokens = end_tokens - start_tokens
        return {
            "decode_throughput_tokens_per_s": measured_tokens / duration,
            "tpot_ms": duration * len(self.counts) / measured_tokens * 1000,
            "window_duration_s": duration,
            "measured_tokens": measured_tokens,
        }


async def stream_batch(
    session: aiohttp.ClientSession,
    base_url: str,
    prompts: list[list[int]],
    indices: list[int],
    counter: DecodeCounter,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> None:
    payload = {
        "input_ids": prompts,
        "sampling_params": {
            "temperature": 0,
            "max_new_tokens": args.output_len,
            "ignore_eos": True,
            "stream_interval": args.stream_interval,
        },
        "stream": True,
    }
    async with session.post(
        base_url.rstrip("/") + "/generate", json=payload
    ) as response:
        if response.status != 200:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{base_url}: HTTP {response.status}: {await response.text()}"
            )
        # SGLang sends one JSON object per SSE data line. Iterating lines handles
        # arbitrary TCP fragmentation without treating network chunks as events.
        async for raw_line in response.content:
            if not raw_line.startswith(b"data:"):
                continue
            now = time.perf_counter()
            data = raw_line[5:].strip()
            if data == b"[DONE]":
                break
            event = orjson.loads(data)
            if "error" in event:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: {event['error']}")
            index = event["index"]
            if not 0 <= index < len(indices):
                raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Invalid request index {index}")
            counter.record(indices[index], event["meta_info"], now)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Stream ended without [DONE]")
    if any(index not in counter.finished for index in indices):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Stream ended before all requests finished")


async def report_prefill_progress(counter: DecodeCounter) -> None:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    total = len(counter.counts)
    while not counter.all_started.is_set():
        print(
            f"Prefill: {counter.num_started}/{total} requests returned first token "
            f"({counter.num_started / total:.1%}); "
            f"elapsed {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f}s",
            flush=True,
        )
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(counter.all_started.wait(), timeout=1)
        except TimeoutError:
            continue
    print(
        f"Prefill: {total}/{total} requests returned first token (100.0%); "
        f"elapsed {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f}s. Collecting decode results.",
        flush=True,
    )


async def benchmark(args: argparse.Namespace, prompts: list[list[int]]) -> dict:
    counter = DecodeCounter(counts=[0] * len(prompts), output_len=args.output_len)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
        timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=6 * 60 * 60), read_bufsize=1024 * 1024
    ) as session:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
            group.create_task(report_prefill_progress(counter))
            for index, base_url in enumerate(args.base_url):
                group.create_task(
                    stream_batch(
                        session,
                        base_url,
                        prompts[index :: len(args.base_url)],
                        list(range(index, len(prompts), len(args.base_url))),
                        counter,
                        args,
                    )
                )
    return counter.result()


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model",
        required=True,
        help="Tokenizer model ID or local path; must match the servers",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--base-url",
        nargs="+",
        default=["http://127.0.0.1:30000"],
        help="Server root URLs sharing one decode schedule; defaults to http://",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--concurrency",
        type=int,
        default=256,
        help="Total requests across all URLs (default: 256)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset",
        choices=("sharegpt", "gsm8k"),
        default="sharegpt",
        help="Prompt source (default: sharegpt); GSM8K uses main/train",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset-path",
        help="Local JSON/JSONL for the selected dataset; otherwise download/cache from Hugging Face",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--input-len",
        type=int,
        help="Exact input tokens, including shared prefix; default: original prompt length",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--prefix-len",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="Shared prefix tokens; requires --input-len (default: 0)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-len",
        type=int,
        default=512,
        help="Generated tokens per request, ignoring EOS (default: 512)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--stream-interval",
        type=int,
        default=8,
        help="Tokens between streaming updates; 1 increases output overhead (default: 8)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--seed", type=int, default=42, help="Dataset shuffle seed (default: 42)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.concurrency <= 0:
        parser.error("Concurrency must be positive")
    if args.stream_interval <= 0:
        parser.error("--stream-interval must be positive")
    if args.output_len < 2:
        parser.error("--output-len must be at least 2 to include decode tokens")
    if args.prefix_len < 0 or (args.prefix_len and args.input_len is None):
        parser.error("A nonnegative --prefix-len requires --input-len when nonzero")
    if args.input_len is not None and args.input_len <= args.prefix_len:
        parser.error("--input-len must exceed --prefix-len")
    if args.concurrency < len(args.base_url):
        parser.error("--concurrency must be at least the number of URLs")
    args.base_url = [
        url if url.startswith(("http://", "https://")) else f"http://{url}"
        for url in args.base_url
    ]
    return args


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    prompts = load_prompts(args)
    lengths = [len(prompt) for prompt in prompts]
    print(
        f"Sending {len(prompts)} {args.dataset} requests across {len(args.base_url)} endpoint(s); "
        f"stream interval: {args.stream_interval}; "
        f"input tokens min/mean/max: {min(lengths)}/{sum(lengths) / len(lengths):.1f}/{max(lengths)}",
        flush=True,
    )
    result = asyncio.run(benchmark(args, prompts))
    print(
        f"Client-observed decode throughput: {result['decode_throughput_tokens_per_s']:.2f} tokens/s"
    )
    print(f"TPOT: {result['tpot_ms']:.2f} ms")
    print(
        f"Window: {result['window_duration_s']:.3f} s, "
        f"{result['measured_tokens']} received tokens"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

<!-- END BENCHMARK SCRIPT -->

</details>

### End-to-end serving with PD disaggregation

On **Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 with 32 SM100 GPUs**, PD + AFD delivers **22.5% higher output throughput at comparable TPOT** (~15 ms), using the same 16-GPU prefill pool and the existing PD serving path.

We use SGLang's serving benchmark with variable-length requests: input and output lengths are sampled uniformly from 80–100% of 8,192 and 2,048 tokens, respectively, without an explicitly shared prefix.

| Deployment | GPUs | Concurrency | Requests | Input throughput/Prefill GPU (tokens/s) | Output throughput/Decode GPU (tokens/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PD: 2P×8 + 2D×8 | 32 | 256 | 2,000 | 3,363.75 | 839.01 | 4,949.08 | 15.13 |
| PD + AFD: 2P×8 + 2A×4 + F×8 | 32 | 320 | 3,000 | 4,115.58 | 1,027.99 | 6,052.73 | 15.09 |

Input throughput is normalized by the 16 prefill GPUs; output throughput is normalized by the 16 decode GPUs, including both A and F for PD + AFD.

<details>
<summary>Deployment and benchmark commands</summary>

Replace the example addresses below. Set `NODE_RANK` to 0 or 1 for each two-host P, D, or F instance; each A uses one four-GPU host.

```bash
PREFILL_1_IP=192.0.2.10
PREFILL_2_IP=192.0.2.20
DECODE_1_IP=192.0.2.30
DECODE_2_IP=192.0.2.40
FFN_MASTER_IP=192.0.2.50
NODE_RANK=0
```

**Prefill: 2 instances, identical for both deployments**

```bash
PREFILL_MASTER_IP="$PREFILL_1_IP"  # Use PREFILL_2_IP for the second instance.

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --tp 8 --attn-dp-size 8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 200 --trust-remote-code \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
  --dist-init-addr "${PREFILL_MASTER_IP}:20000" --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK"
```

**PD decode: 2 instances**

```bash
DECODE_MASTER_IP="$DECODE_1_IP"  # Use DECODE_2_IP for the second instance.

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --tp 8 --port 200 --host 0.0.0.0 --trust-remote-code \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 1536 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.84 \
  --attn-dp-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --dist-init-addr "${DECODE_MASTER_IP}:20000" --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

**PD + AFD attention: 2 instances**

```bash
NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --tp 4 --port 200 --host 0.0.0.0 --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --afd-role attn --afd-ffn-addr "${FFN_MASTER_IP}:200" --afd-backend direct_megamoe \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 1536 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --attn-dp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --afd-decode-num-microbatches 2
```

**PD + AFD FFN: 1 instance**

```bash
NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --tp 8 --port 200 --host 0.0.0.0 --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --afd-role ffn --afd-backend direct_megamoe \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --dist-init-addr "${FFN_MASTER_IP}:20000" --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --afd-attn-instances 2
```

**Router**

The decode endpoints point to D for PD, or A for PD + AFD.

```bash
python -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill "http://${PREFILL_1_IP}:200" 8998 \
  --prefill "http://${PREFILL_2_IP}:200" 8998 \
  --decode "http://${DECODE_1_IP}:200" \
  --decode "http://${DECODE_2_IP}:200" \
  --decode-policy power_of_two
```

**Benchmark**

```bash
CONCURRENCY=256 NUM_PROMPTS=2000  # PD; use 320 and 3000 for PD + AFD.

python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 2048 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --tokenize-prompt --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" \
  --flush-cache
```

</details>

### Execution profile

![Measured A-side microbatch overlap during CUDA Graph replay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3923b55-5a63-4cfc-9a09-f03d877f363f)

A-side PyTorch Profiler trace of Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 on SM100: 2A×4 + F×8, 256 concurrent requests, 8,192 input tokens, and two decode microbatches. Attention and local computation overlap with Megamoe M2N AG kernels across the two microbatches during CUDA Graph replay.

## Follow-up work and maintenance

We will maintain this implementation, follow up on issues and regressions, keep it compatible with upstream changes, and help review community contributions. [Tracking issue #45568](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45568) covers additional model architectures and quantization formats, heterogeneous A/F deployments, and further serving and performance improvements.

We also plan to publish a technical report covering the implementation, deployment experience, simulation-guided A:F sizing, and broader performance results.

Thanks to @Jamesswang, @wtligit, @junparser and @wyzzbond for their contributions to the design, discussions, testing, performance evaluation, and review of AFD.

> Have you benchmarked the colocated baseline with EP16 or higher, rather than EP8? If so, could you share how the throughput per GPU and TPOT compare with AFD under those configurations?

Not yet. The current experiments keep expert parallelism fixed at EP8 while comparing the two execution architectures. The current results are specific to these configurations; scaling both systems while keeping per-attention-rank concurrency and AFD’s attention-to-FFN GPU ratio fixed could improve expert batching efficiency in both. The relative gains will also depend on communication overhead and changes in the compute bottlenecks. We plan to explore larger-EP deployments as part of a forthcoming paper and share those results when available.

Thanks for clarifying. Could you also benchmark a 16-GPU colocated EP16 baseline against AFD with 8 attention GPUs + 8 FFN GPUs (2A×4 + F×8)? Both deployments would use the same total of 16 GPUs. It would be useful to compare their throughput at similar TPOT under this equal-GPU-budget setup, rather than keeping EP fixed at 8.

> Thanks for clarifying. Could you also benchmark a 16-GPU colocated EP16 baseline against AFD with 8 attention GPUs + 8 FFN GPUs (2A×4 + F×8)? Both deployments would use the same total of 16 GPUs. It would be useful to compare their throughput at similar TPOT under this equal-GPU-budget setup, rather than keeping EP fixed at 8. Thanks for the suggestion. I just ran an additional EP16 experiment on SM100 with Qwen3-235B. Scaling colocate to EP16 improves per-GPU throughput and brings it on par with AFD at the same GPU budget. The larger aggregate batch gives each expert more tokens to process, which can improve GEMM efficiency—the same batching effect that AFD aims to exploit by pooling tokens from multiple attention instances. We also scaled AFD’s FFN group to EP16. This further improved per-GPU throughput. A key motivation for homogeneous AFD is to feed experts with larger batches while keeping attention-side concurrency manageable. Its potential advantage lies in independently tuning attention and FFN capacity to match their different computational characteristics. These AFD results keep the A:F GPU ratio fixed. As expert execution becomes more efficient while attention-side remains unchanged, the bottleneck can shift toward attention. The optimal A:F ratio may therefore change with deployment scale.

Thanks for running these additional experiments and sharing the results! Looking forward to more benchmark results and analysis.

One more question: for hybrid-attention models such as DeepSeek-V4, could differences in attention execution time across layers introduce additional pipeline bubbles in AFD? If the FFN workload is similar across layers while attention latency varies, I wonder whether this could leave the A or F side idle more often and reduce the effectiveness of microbatch overlap. Have you observed or profiled this effect?

One additional question: was MegaMoE also enabled for the colocated baselines, including the EP8 and newly tested EP16 configurations? Or did they use DeepEP dispatch/combine with separate expert compute kernels?

> Thanks for running these additional experiments and sharing the results! Looking forward to more benchmark results and analysis.
> 
> One more question: for hybrid-attention models such as DeepSeek-V4, could differences in attention execution time across layers introduce additional pipeline bubbles in AFD? If the FFN workload is similar across layers while attention latency varies, I wonder whether this could leave the A or F side idle more often and reduce the effectiveness of microbatch overlap. Have you observed or profiled this effect?

Yes, we have looked at this in our DeepSeek-V4-Pro profiling. The ratio-4/indexer and ratio-128 layers show different timing and dependency patterns at microbatch handoffs, so the pipeline balance does vary across layers. We also observed overlap across microbatches despite this variation.

The concern is valid: a fixed microbatch configuration cannot necessarily hide the latency variation of every layer.

Thanks for confirming. Would you be able to share the DeepSeek-V4-Pro profiling trace, or representative timeline screenshots covering both the A and F sides? It would be helpful to see the pipeline bubble/idle-time fraction across different layer types, particularly the ratio-4/indexer and ratio-128 layers, and how much attention, communication, and expert computation actually overlap across microbatches. Please also include the A:F GPU configuration, concurrency, and microbatch count used for the profile.

> One additional question: was MegaMoE also enabled for the colocated baselines, including the EP8 and newly tested EP16 configurations? Or did they use DeepEP dispatch/combine with separate expert compute kernels?

Both colocated configurations used DeepEP dispatch/combine with separate expert compute kernels. Native MegaMoE does not currently support the Qwen3 block-FP8 checkpoint on SM100 through SGLang’s integration.

The performance gains reported in the PR are relative to the stated DeepEP baselines. This PR introduces the AFD execution path and the ability to provision attention and FFN resources independently. We will continue refining the kernels and share further performance analysis across deployment configurations and execution backends.

To make the implementation easier to review, we propose upstreaming AFD through a series of smaller PRs. The design and proposed breakdown are in #45568. Feedback on the runtime interfaces, PR boundaries, and ordering would be welcome.

We will keep this PR as the complete implementation and benchmark reference while preparing the incremental PRs, and track those PRs in #45568. The existing DeepEP and DeepGEMM PRs can continue to be reviewed in parallel.

@ShangmingCai Could you take a look at this AFD implementation and advise on the preferred integration path?

This PR contains the complete implementation, with accuracy and performance results and reproduction instructions. We would be happy to proceed with reviewing it as a whole if that works for the maintainers.

To make incremental review possible, we have also outlined a breakdown in RFC #45568 and opened the first PR, #45958, covering the core framework and asymmetric parallelism. The remaining capabilities are already implemented here and can follow as smaller PRs.

Feedback on both the design and the preferred review scope would be appreciated.

We optimized the activation cache policy and moved routing weight and return metadata loads earlier in the MegaMoE M2N expert kernel to better hide memory latency in sgl-project/DeepGEMM#110.

In the tested configurations, we observed up to **3.3% higher decode throughput** and a **2.6–4.7% speedup in FP8 M2N microbenchmarks**, including communication.

The performance results currently shown in this PR were measured before this optimization.

Added support for **Qwen3.5 MOE**, including multimodal inputs and its hybrid Gated DeltaNet/full-attention architecture.We measured **2.67× decode throughput per GPU at comparable TPOT** versus the colocated EP8 baseline. Accuracy and performance results for text workloads are included in the updated PR description.

detail.body:
## Motivation

MoE inference normally places attention and routed experts on the same GPU group. This PR adds Attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD), allowing them to run on separate groups. Multiple attention instances can share one FFN instance and its routed-expert weights, so attention capacity can grow without replicating those weights for every instance.

Requests continue to use SGLang's serving APIs on the attention instances. AFD is opt-in through `--afd-role`.

![SGLang AFD: tokens from multiple attention instances form shared expert batches, and Megamoe M2N overlaps attention with remote expert execution across microbatches and layers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd4e8f84-4272-4fee-a4a4-3b7e7df6d54c)

F batches routed tokens across A instances. In the Megamoe M2N decode path, per-microbatch communication lanes overlap with attention computation, while one persistent kernel per F rank processes successive layers and microbatches. Timing in the diagram is schematic.

## Modifications

- Add attention (A) and FFN (F) roles, startup handshakes, role-specific weight loading, and remote expert execution. A owns requests, KV cache, attention, routing, shared experts, and sampling; F owns routed experts.
- Support asymmetric A/F parallelism, CUDA graphs, decode microbatch overlap, and batching across attention instances sharing F. F graph and dispatch capacities are derived from the attention handshakes.
- Provide staged NCCL and NVSHMEM transports, Direct DeepEP, and Megamoe M2N. NCCL uses standard SGLang dependencies; other backends load their optional components only when selected.
- Integrate Qwen3 MoE, Qwen3.5 MoE, DeepSeek V3/V3.2/V4, and the GLM-5 MoE DSA family, including EAGLE/MTP and DSpark with draft execution on A.
- Add coverage to the registered CPU test suites, an AFD deployment guide, and a DeepSeek-V4-Pro Megamoe M2N recipe.

### Usage and scope

Start attention workers with `--afd-role attn --afd-ffn-addr <ffn-host>:<port>` and FFN workers with `--afd-role ffn`. For a shared F, set `--afd-attn-instances` to the number of attention instances. Send generation requests to A.

Complete deployment examples and the backend/precision support matrix are in `docs/docs/advanced_features/afd_disaggregation.mdx`. The multi-host Pro recipe is in `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx`.

The initial implementation uses fixed membership established at startup and homogeneous attention instances, with TP size one within each attention DP group. Direct backends require pure expert parallelism on F. Direct MegaMoE requires SM100/SM103 GPUs with peer-accessible memory; cross-host execution requires a shared NVLink fabric with CUDA FABRIC access. The deployment guide lists the remaining feature combinations and restrictions.

<details>
<summary>Optional components</summary>

Install the component required by the selected backend on all participating workers.

| Backend | Package / required API | Public source and release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nccl` | Standard SGLang dependencies | No additional AFD component |
| `nvshmem` | `afd-nvshmem` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/afd-nvshmem/tree/15a7764608f8211e6a564270608fb53e23e5a591) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/afd-nvshmem/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261019) |
| `direct_deepep` | `sgl-deep-ep` exposing `deep_ep.afd` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepEP/tree/dcd018ba3e1a6d4f892eb9cd8a10e73dfb8bb54d) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepEP/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261019) |
| `direct_megamoe` | `sgl-deep-gemm` exposing `deep_gemm.mega.m2n` | [Source](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/tree/991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c) · [Wheels](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/releases/tag/afd-preview-20261028) |

The AFD DeepEP build also provides the standard DeepEP APIs. The required AFD extensions are not yet included in the official component wheels.

Related component PRs: [DeepEP #14](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepEP/pull/14) (target `sgl-deepep`) and [DeepGEMM #110](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/110) (target `dev`).

The M2N component adapts code from [FastAFD](https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/FastAFD/tree/3c7161949310b6d59d6b4cf9bf997a4935c8113b). Source attribution and original copyright/license notices are retained in the component repository and package.

</details>

## Accuracy Tests

For each model, we compare colocated inference and AFD using identical evaluation prompts, checkpoints, quantization, and sampling parameters. Source revisions and evaluation settings are listed below. Speculative decoding uses actual acceptance without simulation.

| GPU architecture | Model | Benchmark | Colocate (%) | AFD (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| SM103 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | GSM8K | 94.84 | 95.07 |
| SM103 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | GPQA Diamond | 87.12 ± 1.20 | 86.74 ± 2.04 |
| SM100 | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GSM8K | 95.91 | 96.51 |
| SM100 | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GPQA Diamond | 69.44 ± 0.87 | 69.82 ± 1.51 |
| SM103 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | GSM8K | 97.12 | 97.57 |
| SM103 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | GPQA Diamond | 88.01 ± 1.95 | 88.51 ± 0.76 |
| SM100 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 | GSM8K | 90.90 | 90.90 |
| SM100 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 | GPQA Diamond | 87.12 ± 0.65 | 88.38 ± 1.24 |

- GSM8K: all 1,319 test questions, 0-shot, one run with seed 0.
- GPQA Diamond: all 198 questions, 0-shot, `--n-repeats 4`, without a fixed seed. Results are mean accuracy ± standard deviation across the four repetitions.
- Evaluation concurrency: 256. Evaluator: `sgl-eval==0.1.2`.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation parameters</summary>

| Parameter | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reasoning mode | Thinking, `reasoning_effort=high` | `enable_thinking=true` | `enable_thinking=true` | `enable_thinking=true` |
| Temperature | 1.0 | 0.6 | 1.0 | 0.6 |
| `top_p` | 1.0 | 0.95 | 0.95 | 0.95 |
| `top_k` | Unrestricted | 20 | Unrestricted | 20 |
| `min_p` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Maximum output tokens, including reasoning | 65,536 | 30,000 | 65,536 | 32,768 |

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Decode-only

ShareGPT prompts with 8,192 input tokens, a 90% shared prefix, and 512 output tokens.

For the SM100/SM103 results below, we compare colocated EP8/attention-DP8 using DeepEP with AFD attention TP4/attention-DP4 instances sharing EP8 FFN workers. Both use attention TP1 per DP rank. AFD decode uses Megamoe M2N; F uses DeepEP for staged prefill. Throughput per GPU includes every GPU in the deployment, including A and F. Each marker below is a measured configuration; lines connect the selected points as visual guides.

The DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3-235B, and GLM-5.2 results predate the [M2N memory-access optimization](https://github.com/sunfanyi/DeepGEMM/commit/991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c) and retain their original measurements and source revisions. The Qwen3.5 results use this optimization. Separate measurements showed up to **3.3% higher decode throughput** from the optimization in the tested configurations.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED PERFORMANCE SUMMARY -->

Selected comparisons at similar TPOT (colocate → AFD):

- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 1.52× throughput/GPU**, at 10.32 → 10.22 ms.
- **Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8: 2.68× throughput/GPU**, at 14.36 → 14.30 ms.
- **GLM-5.2-NVFP4: 1.78× throughput/GPU**, at 6.87 → 6.85 ms.
- **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8: 2.67× throughput/GPU**, at 17.33 → 17.32 ms.

<!-- END GENERATED PERFORMANCE SUMMARY -->

![Decode throughput per GPU versus TPOT for DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, and GLM-5.2-NVFP4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/710d6285-4971-4e31-9f91-7cda724f59f4)

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

The Qwen3.5 accuracy and performance results cover text workloads and use the Qwen3.5/AFD implementation corresponding to SGLang `932ba87c338f31888c4da8e823112ad67b0aa2fc` and DeepGEMM `991584b2e8496a927ebe5b8fdfb518babb3a9c9c`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""Measure fixed-batch decode throughput with SGLang's streaming API.

Requires Python 3.11+. Dependencies:
    pip install aiohttp transformers huggingface_hub orjson
    pip install datasets  # Only needed to download GSM8K.

Example:
    python bench_decode.py --model /path/to/model --concurrency 256 \
        --base-url 127.0.0.1:30000 --input-len 8192 --prefix-len 7373

The default dataset is ShareGPT. --dataset gsm8k uses openai/gsm8k, configuration
main, split train. Both download through the Hugging Face cache unless a local
JSON/JSONL --dataset-path is given. Prompts use ShareGPT's first conversation turn
or GSM8K's question field, without a chat template. Explicit input lengths
repeat/truncate token IDs; the shared prefix is part of that length.

All requests must fit concurrently, and all prefill must finish before decode
starts. All URLs must share one coordinated decode schedule.

Record the total received token count when every request has returned tokens,
then again when the first request finishes. Throughput is the count difference
divided by the elapsed client time. Counts come directly from streaming metadata,
without interpolation. HTTP delivery order can shift the boundaries relative to
GPU steps; this is client-observed throughput, not exact GPU timing.
TPOT is concurrency / throughput, expressed in milliseconds for this window.
Streaming updates are buffered every 8 tokens by default to avoid output-path
backlog at high concurrency. Counts still come from cumulative metadata; no
interpolation is used. --stream-interval 1 requests per-token updates.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import random
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import aiohttp
import orjson

SHAREGPT_REPO = "anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered"
SHAREGPT_FILE = "ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json"


def resize_tokens(tokens: list[int], length: int) -> list[int]:
    return (tokens * ((length + len(tokens) - 1) // len(tokens)))[:length]


def load_dataset_rows(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[dict]:
    if args.dataset == "gsm8k" and not args.dataset_path:
        from datasets import load_dataset

        return list(load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="train"))

    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

    dataset_path = args.dataset_path or hf_hub_download(
        repo_id=SHAREGPT_REPO, filename=SHAREGPT_FILE, repo_type="dataset"
    )
    with open(dataset_path) as f:
        if dataset_path.endswith(".jsonl"):
            return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
        return json.load(f)


def load_prompts(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[list[int]]:
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    dataset = load_dataset_rows(args)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
    random.Random(args.seed).shuffle(dataset)

    prompts = []
    prefix = []
    for row in dataset:
        if args.dataset == "gsm8k":
            text = row["question"]
        else:
            conversation = row.get("conversations", row.get("conversation", []))
            if len(conversation) < 2:
                continue
            text = conversation[0]["value"]
        tokens = tokenizer.encode(text)
        if len(tokens) < 2:
            continue
        if args.prefix_len and not prefix:
            prefix = resize_tokens(tokens, args.prefix_len)
            continue
        if args.input_len is not None:
            tokens = resize_tokens(tokens, args.input_len - args.prefix_len)
        prompts.append(prefix + tokens)
        if len(prompts) == args.concurrency:
            return prompts
    raise ValueError(f"Dataset has only {len(prompts)} usable prompts")


@dataclass
class DecodeCounter:
    counts: list[int]
    output_len: int
    finished: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    num_started: int = 0
    total_tokens: int = 0
    all_started: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
    start: tuple[float, int] | None = None
    end: tuple[float, int] | None = None

    def record(self, index: int, meta: dict, now: float) -> None:
        count = meta["completion_tokens"]
        previous = self.counts[index]
        if index in self.finished or not previous <= count <= self.output_len:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid token progress: {previous} -> {count}")
        self.total_tokens += count - previous
        self.counts[index] = count
        if previous == 0 and count > 0:
            self.num_started += 1
            if self.num_started == len(self.counts):
                self.start = (now, self.total_tokens)
                self.all_started.set()
        reason = meta["finish_reason"]
        if reason is not None:
            if reason["type"] != "length" or count != self.output_len:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Incomplete generation: {count} tokens, {reason}")
            self.finished.add(index)
            if self.end is None:
                self.end = (now, self.total_tokens)

    def result(self) -> dict:
        if (
            len(self.finished) != len(self.counts)
            or self.start is None
            or self.end is None
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Every request must produce tokens and finish successfully"
            )
        start_time, start_tokens = self.start
        end_time, end_tokens = self.end
        if end_time <= start_time or end_tokens <= start_tokens:
            raise ValueError(
                "No common decode window: a request finished before all started"
            )
        duration = end_time - start_time
        measured_tokens = end_tokens - start_tokens
        return {
            "decode_throughput_tokens_per_s": measured_tokens / duration,
            "tpot_ms": duration * len(self.counts) / measured_tokens * 1000,
            "window_duration_s": duration,
            "measured_tokens": measured_tokens,
        }


async def stream_batch(
    session: aiohttp.ClientSession,
    base_url: str,
    prompts: list[list[int]],
    indices: list[int],
    counter: DecodeCounter,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> None:
    payload = {
        "input_ids": prompts,
        "sampling_params": {
            "temperature": 0,
            "max_new_tokens": args.output_len,
            "ignore_eos": True,
            "stream_interval": args.stream_interval,
        },
        "stream": True,
    }
    async with session.post(
        base_url.rstrip("/") + "/generate", json=payload
    ) as response:
        if response.status != 200:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{base_url}: HTTP {response.status}: {await response.text()}"
            )
        # SGLang sends one JSON object per SSE data line. Iterating lines handles
        # arbitrary TCP fragmentation without treating network chunks as events.
        async for raw_line in response.content:
            if not raw_line.startswith(b"data:"):
                continue
            now = time.perf_counter()
            data = raw_line[5:].strip()
            if data == b"[DONE]":
                break
            event = orjson.loads(data)
            if "error" in event:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: {event['error']}")
            index = event["index"]
            if not 0 <= index < len(indices):
                raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Invalid request index {index}")
            counter.record(indices[index], event["meta_info"], now)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Stream ended without [DONE]")
    if any(index not in counter.finished for index in indices):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{base_url}: Stream ended before all requests finished")


async def report_prefill_progress(counter: DecodeCounter) -> None:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    total = len(counter.counts)
    while not counter.all_started.is_set():
        print(
            f"Prefill: {counter.num_started}/{total} requests returned first token "
            f"({counter.num_started / total:.1%}); "
            f"elapsed {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f}s",
            flush=True,
        )
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(counter.all_started.wait(), timeout=1)
        except TimeoutError:
            continue
    print(
        f"Prefill: {total}/{total} requests returned first token (100.0%); "
        f"elapsed {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f}s. Collecting decode results.",
        flush=True,
    )


async def benchmark(args: argparse.Namespace, prompts: list[list[int]]) -> dict:
    counter = DecodeCounter(counts=[0] * len(prompts), output_len=args.output_len)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
        timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=6 * 60 * 60), read_bufsize=1024 * 1024
    ) as session:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
            group.create_task(report_prefill_progress(counter))
            for index, base_url in enumerate(args.base_url):
                group.create_task(
                    stream_batch(
                        session,
                        base_url,
                        prompts[index :: len(args.base_url)],
                        list(range(index, len(prompts), len(args.base_url))),
                        counter,
                        args,
                    )
                )
    return counter.result()


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model",
        required=True,
        help="Tokenizer model ID or local path; must match the servers",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--base-url",
        nargs="+",
        default=["http://127.0.0.1:30000"],
        help="Server root URLs sharing one decode schedule; defaults to http://",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--concurrency",
        type=int,
        default=256,
        help="Total requests across all URLs (default: 256)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset",
        choices=("sharegpt", "gsm8k"),
        default="sharegpt",
        help="Prompt source (default: sharegpt); GSM8K uses main/train",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset-path",
        help="Local JSON/JSONL for the selected dataset; otherwise download/cache from Hugging Face",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--input-len",
        type=int,
        help="Exact input tokens, including shared prefix; default: original prompt length",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--prefix-len",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="Shared prefix tokens; requires --input-len (default: 0)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-len",
        type=int,
        default=512,
        help="Generated tokens per request, ignoring EOS (default: 512)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--stream-interval",
        type=int,
        default=8,
        help="Tokens between streaming updates; 1 increases output overhead (default: 8)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--seed", type=int, default=42, help="Dataset shuffle seed (default: 42)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.concurrency <= 0:
        parser.error("Concurrency must be positive")
    if args.stream_interval <= 0:
        parser.error("--stream-interval must be positive")
    if args.output_len < 2:
        parser.error("--output-len must be at least 2 to include decode tokens")
    if args.prefix_len < 0 or (args.prefix_len and args.input_len is None):
        parser.error("A nonnegative --prefix-len requires --input-len when nonzero")
    if args.input_len is not None and args.input_len <= args.prefix_len:
        parser.error("--input-len must exceed --prefix-len")
    if args.concurrency < len(args.base_url):
        parser.error("--concurrency must be at least the number of URLs")
    args.base_url = [
        url if url.startswith(("http://", "https://")) else f"http://{url}"
        for url in args.base_url
    ]
    return args


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    prompts = load_prompts(args)
    lengths = [len(prompt) for prompt in prompts]
    print(
        f"Sending {len(prompts)} {args.dataset} requests across {len(args.base_url)} endpoint(s); "
        f"stream interval: {args.stream_interval}; "
        f"input tokens min/mean/max: {min(lengths)}/{sum(lengths) / len(lengths):.1f}/{max(lengths)}",
        flush=True,
    )
    result = asyncio.run(benchmark(args, prompts))
    print(
        f"Client-observed decode throughput: {result['decode_throughput_tokens_per_s']:.2f} tokens/s"
    )
    print(f"TPOT: {result['tpot_ms']:.2f} ms")
    print(
        f"Window: {result['window_duration_s']:.3f} s, "
        f"{result['measured_tokens']} received tokens"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  --afd-role ffn --afd-backend direct_megamoe \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --dist-init-addr "${FFN_MASTER_IP}:20000" --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --afd-attn-instances 2
```

**Router**

The decode endpoints point to D for PD, or A for PD + AFD.

```bash
python -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill "http://${PREFILL_1_IP}:200" 8998 \
  --prefill "http://${PREFILL_2_IP}:200" 8998 \
  --decode "http://${DECODE_1_IP}:200" \
  --decode "http://${DECODE_2_IP}:200" \
  --decode-policy power_of_two
```

**Benchmark**

```bash
CONCURRENCY=256 NUM_PROMPTS=2000  # PD; use 320 and 3000 for PD + AFD.

python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 2048 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --tokenize-prompt --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" \
  --flush-cache
```

</details>

### Execution profile

![Measured A-side microbatch overlap during CUDA Graph replay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3923b55-5a63-4cfc-9a09-f03d877f363f)

A-side PyTorch Profiler trace of Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 on SM100: 2A×4 + F×8, 256 concurrent requests, 8,192 input tokens, and two decode microbatches. Attention and local computation overlap with Megamoe M2N AG kernels across the two microbatches during CUDA Graph replay.

## Follow-up work and maintenance

We will maintain this implementation, follow up on issues and regressions, keep it compatible with upstream changes, and help review community contributions. [Tracking issue #45568](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45568) covers additional model architectures and quantization formats, heterogeneous A/F deployments, and further serving and performance improvements.

We also plan to publish a technical report covering the implementation, deployment experience, simulation-guided A:F sizing, and broader performance results.

Thanks to @Jamesswang, @wtligit, @junparser and @wyzzbond for their contributions to the design, discussions, testing, performance evaluation, and review of AFD.

+---
+title: "Attention-FFN disaggregation"
+description: "Run attention and routed MoE experts on separate GPU groups with AFD."
+---
+
+Attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) separates routed MoE expert computation from
+the rest of the model. The attention instance (A) owns request scheduling,
+attention, KV cache, routing, and shared experts. The FFN instance (F) owns routed
+expert weights and executes the expert work sent by A at each MoE layer. Send
+generation requests to A; F does not serve generation requests.
+
+Multiple A instances can share one F instance. You can choose their GPU counts
+independently, subject to the parallelism requirements below.
+
+For a multi-host deployment with shared experts, EAGLE/MTP, and decode microbatch
+overlap, see the [DeepSeek-V4-Pro Direct MegaMoE recipe on GB300](/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4#3-9-attention-ffn-disaggregation-on-gb300).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Linux with NVIDIA GPUs and a working CUDA 13
+  [SGLang installation](/docs/get-started/install).
+- The same SGLang revision containing AFD support and the same model checkpoint
+  on A and F. Use matching optional component builds on all workers when
+  selecting an optional backend.
+- Network connectivity between all participating workers. On multiple hosts, use
+  an F address reachable from every A worker. The handshake uses F's API port
+  plus 300, and workers also establish NCCL and control connections.
+
+## Supported models and precisions
+
+AFD integrates Qwen3 MoE, DeepSeek V3/V3.2/V4, and the GLM-5 MoE DSA family. These
+architectures also support AFD decode microbatch overlap.
+
+Quantization support depends on the AFD backend and F's MoE runner. The table
+describes **routed-expert weight formats**; attention, shared experts, and KV
+cache can use different formats.
+
+| Backend | Routed-expert weights | Model activation dtype |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `nccl` / `nvshmem` | BF16, FP8, MXFP4, or ModelOpt NVFP4, where supported by the model and native F MoE runner | Must match between A and F |
+| `direct_deepep` | FP8 or MXFP4 with the DeepGEMM core; ModelOpt NVFP4 with `flashinfer_cutedsl` | BF16 |
+| `direct_megamoe` | 128×128 block FP8, MXFP4, or ModelOpt NVFP4 with prepared MegaMoE weights | BF16 |
+
+The Direct backends require BF16 model activations but do not support BF16
+routed-expert weights. Direct MegaMoE additionally requires SM100 or SM103 GPUs.
+MXFP4 includes the routed-expert format used by DeepSeek V4; it does not imply
+that every layer runs in FP4. FP8 support is limited to the layouts accepted by
+the selected runner, and does not imply MXFP8 support.
+
+These are implementation capabilities. Accuracy and performance qualification
+applies to specific model, checkpoint, backend, and hardware configurations.
+
+## Select a backend
+
+`nccl` is the default backend. To select another backend, set the same
+`--afd-backend` on A and F.
+
+| Backend | Decode path | Additional AFD component |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `nccl` | Staged transfers between A and F | None |
+| `nvshmem` | Transfers through a shared symmetric arena | `afd-nvshmem` |
+| `direct_deepep` | Direct token dispatch from A ranks to F expert owners | An `sgl-deep-ep` build exposing `deep_ep.afd` |
+| `direct_megamoe` | Fused M2N dispatch, expert compute, and combine | An `sgl-deep-gemm` build exposing `deep_gemm.mega.m2n` |
+
+All backends use staged NCCL transfers for prefill. For staged backends,
+`--moe-a2a-backend` selects F's internal expert layout; set it consistently on A
+and F. The default is `none`. To use DeepEP within F, select `deepep` on both
+sides and configure F's expert parallelism.
+
+Direct backends configure this internal layout automatically. They require pure
+expert parallelism on F (`--ep-size` equal to `--tp`, with `--moe-dp-size 1`) and
+either `deep_gemm` or `flashinfer_cutedsl` as its MoE runner, depending on the
+model's quantization. Direct MegaMoE requires trivial expert placement and no
+redundant experts.
+
+### Install optional components
+
+Install only the component needed for your selected backend. Use wheels built
+for your Python version, CPU architecture, Torch, and CUDA environment. These
+AFD component builds are separate from the standard SGLang installation; a stock
+DeepGEMM wheel does not provide the M2N API.
+
+The standard `sgl-deep-ep` package provides legacy `deep_ep.Buffer` and v2
+`deep_ep.ElasticBuffer` for the `deepep` and `deepep_v2` MoE backends.
+AFD's `direct_deepep` uses additional native bindings from `deep_ep.afd` in
+the same package. Current official wheels do not include these AFD extensions.
+
+{/* TODO: Add public source and release links once component publishing is finalized. */}
+
+Replace the local paths below with the corresponding wheel paths:
+
+```bash
+# For --afd-backend nvshmem:
+python -m pip install --no-deps /path/to/afd_nvshmem-*.whl
+
+# For --afd-backend direct_deepep:
+python -m pip install --no-deps /path/to/sgl_deep_ep-*.whl
+
+# For --afd-backend direct_megamoe:
+python -m pip install --no-deps /path/to/sgl_deep_gemm-*.whl
+```
+
+Use AFD-tagged versions for the modified DeepEP and DeepGEMM builds to distinguish
+them from stock releases. The AFD DeepEP wheel replaces the standard
+`sgl-deep-ep` wheel and also supplies F's DeepEP prefill path. The private NVSHMEM
+runtime allows its AFD path to coexist with standard DeepEP.
+
+## Reference deployment
+
+The following single-host baseline deploys Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 on four NVIDIA GB300
+GPUs. It uses the default staged NCCL backend and standard SGLang
+dependencies. Each GPU group must have enough memory for its model weights;
+A also needs capacity for KV cache and concurrent requests.
+
+| Instance | GPUs | Parallelism | Endpoint |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Attention | 0, 1 | TP2 with attention DP2 | `127.0.0.1:30000` (default) |
+| FFN | 2, 3 | TP2 | `127.0.0.1:31000` |
+
+The commands specify only the model, topology, roles, and F endpoint. Memory
+allocation, context length, request capacity, kernel selection, and CUDA graph
+configuration use SGLang defaults. The A:F allocation is a deployment baseline;
+size and tune it against the workload before using it as a production configuration.
+
+### Attention instance
+
+Start A on its assigned GPUs and connect it to F's API address. With `--tp 2`,
+AFD requires `--attn-dp-size 2` so that each attention group has TP size one.
+
+```bash
+MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8
+
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+  --tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2 \
+  --afd-role attn \
+  --afd-ffn-addr 127.0.0.1:31000
+```
+
+### FFN instance
+
+Start F on its assigned GPUs. The nondefault port separates F from A on the
+same host.
+
+```bash
+MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8
+
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+  --tp 2 \
+  --afd-role ffn \
+  --port 31000
+```
+
+### Service readiness
+
+Start both A and F. Once model initialization, the AFD handshake, and CUDA graph
+capture complete, validate the generation path through A's endpoint:
+
+```bash
+curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  -d '{"text":"The capital of France is","sampling_params":{"temperature":0,"max_new_tokens":32}}'
+```
+
+F's HTTP readiness alone does not establish that the AFD group is ready to serve.
+For a multi-host deployment, use an F address reachable by all A workers. If an
+individual A or F instance spans hosts, configure `--nnodes`, `--node-rank`, and
+`--dist-init-addr` for that instance separately; `--afd-ffn-addr` still identifies
+F's API endpoint.
+
+## Parallelism and batching
+
+- **A parallelism:** when `--tp` is greater than one, set `--attn-dp-size` to the
+  same value. Each attention group has tensor parallel size one. Leave A's
+  expert-parallel and MoE DP sizes at their defaults of one.
+- **F parallelism:** configure tensor and expert parallelism on F. Do not enable
+  attention DP or model DP on F.
+- **Shared F:** set `--afd-attn-instances` on F to the number of A instances that
+  will connect. Every instance must complete its handshake before serving
+  starts. Staged backends batch compatible ready steps across A instances;
+  direct backends use a joint world across all participating ranks. The A
+  instances must have matching GPU counts, token and graph buckets, and
+  microbatch configurations.
+- **Decode overlap:** set `--afd-decode-num-microbatches 2` or `3` on A to overlap
+  microbatches. The default is `1`. All A instances sharing F must use the same
+  microbatch count. Values greater than one require attention DP greater than
+  one and do not support LoRA.
+
+Keep capacity settings at their defaults unless the workload requires an
+override. Configure request admission and decode graph sizes on A; AFD derives
+F's graph capacities and applicable DeepEP dispatch limits from the handshakes.
+Do not copy A's request or graph limits to F. Configure speculative decoding
+only on A.
+
+For multiple A instances, start all declared instances before waiting for the
+group to become ready. Membership and capacity plans are established at startup;
+restart the A/F group together after changing its topology or capacity settings.
+
+## Current restrictions
+
+- Pipeline parallelism, attention context parallelism, prefill context
+  parallelism, EPLB, waterfill, PD multiplexing, and native two-batch or
+  single-batch overlap are not supported. AFD has its own decode overlap path.
+- AFD disables shared-expert fusion and prefill CUDA graphs. Direct backends
+  select full decode graphs when graphs are enabled and do not support
+  `--enable-torch-compile`.
+- EAGLE and DSPARK integration uses draft-local computation on A. Configure
+  speculative decoding only on A, with `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`, fixed draft
+  token counts, and full decode graphs. Adaptive speculation, multilayer EAGLE,
+  decoupled speculation, and skipping DP MLP synchronization are not supported.
+- An A instance can use PD's `decode` role; F must use
+  `--disaggregation-mode null`. This is separate from the single-host example
+  above; see [PD disaggregation](/docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation).

+"""AFD (Attention-FFN Disaggregation).
+
+Splits attention and MoE expert computation onto separately launched
+instances. The attn instance runs the full model except routed experts;
+the ffn instance serves expert computation for every MoE layer.
+
+All AFD-specific logic lives in this package; existing files only carry
+thin entry-point branches.
+"""
+
+from sglang.srt.afd.afd_config import AFDRole, afd_role_from_args
+
+__all__ = ["AFDRole", "afd_role_from_args"]

@@ -0,0 +1,644 @@
+"""AFD role definition and server-args validation.
+
+The role is derived from ``ServerArgs.afd_role`` so every process spawned
+with the same args agrees on it without extra plumbing.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional
+
+from sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides import (
+    declare_resolution,
+    model_config_of,
+    resolving_view,
+)
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_DEFAULT_COMM_SM_BUDGETS = {
+    "nccl": 8,
+    "nvshmem": 2,
+    "direct_deepep": 24,
+    "direct_megamoe": 24,
+}
+
+_DIRECT_AFD_BACKENDS = frozenset({"direct_deepep", "direct_megamoe"})
+
+
+class AFDRole(Enum):
+    ATTN = "attn"
+    FFN = "ffn"
+
+    def is_attn(self) -> bool:
+        return self == AFDRole.ATTN
+
+    def is_ffn(self) -> bool:
+        return self == AFDRole.FFN
+
+
+def afd_role_from_args(server_args: ServerArgs) -> Optional[AFDRole]:
+    if server_args.afd_role is None:
+        return None
+    return AFDRole(server_args.afd_role)
+
+
+def is_direct_afd_backend(backend: str) -> bool:
+    return backend in _DIRECT_AFD_BACKENDS
+
+
+def requires_afd_mega_moe_weights() -> bool:
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_disagg
+
+    server_args = get_disagg()
+    role = afd_role_from_args(server_args)
+    return (
+        role is not None
+        and role.is_ffn()
+        and server_args.afd_backend == "direct_megamoe"
+    )
+
+
+def resolve_overlap_sm_partition(
+    *,
+    total_num_sms: int,
+    num_microbatches: int,
+    overlap_sm_budget: int,
+    direct_deepep_communication_num_sms_per_lane: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    communication_num_sms = overlap_sm_budget
+    if direct_deepep_communication_num_sms_per_lane is not None:
+        # The compute lane is between its dispatch and combine, so only the
+        # other lanes can own communication CTAs concurrently.
+        communication_num_sms = (
+            num_microbatches - 1
+        ) * direct_deepep_communication_num_sms_per_lane
+
+    compute_num_sms = total_num_sms - communication_num_sms
+    if compute_num_sms <= 0 or compute_num_sms % 2 != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "AFD overlap requires a positive, even compute SM count: "
+            f"total={total_num_sms}, reserved={communication_num_sms}, "
+            f"compute={compute_num_sms}"
+        )
+    return compute_num_sms, communication_num_sms
+
+
+def normalize_afd_ffn_speculative_args(server_args: ServerArgs) -> None:
+    """Ignore speculative decoding arguments on the expert-only F instance."""
+    role = afd_role_from_args(server_args)
+    if role is None or not role.is_ffn():

+
+Runs over ZMQ REQ (attn) / ROUTER (ffn). Users only deal with server API
+addresses: the attn
+side points ``--afd-ffn-addr`` at the ffn instance's ``--host:--port``, and
+both sides derive the internal handshake port from the ffn API port with a
+fixed delta (same pattern as ``ZMQ_TCP_PORT_DELTA``). Startup order is
+arbitrary (the attn request is queued until the ffn side binds).
+Exchanges identity/topology so that every later mismatch (different model,
+different backend, incompatible world sizes) fails loudly at startup
+instead of hanging mid-forward.
+"""

+import bisect
+import hashlib
+import logging
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Sequence, Tuple

+from sglang.srt.afd.dispatcher import (
+    build_decode_token_buckets,

+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils.network import get_zmq_socket

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+# users never configure an extra port (cf. ZMQ_TCP_PORT_DELTA in server_args).

+SYNC_PORT_OFFSET = 1

+def afd_handshake_port(ffn_api_port: int) -> int:
+    port = ffn_api_port + AFD_HANDSHAKE_PORT_DELTA
+    if port + DIST_PORT_OFFSET > 65535:
+        port = ffn_api_port - AFD_HANDSHAKE_PORT_DELTA
+    return port

+@dataclass
+class AFDHandshakeInfo:
+    role: str  # AFDRole value
+    model_identity: str
+    # Number of data-plane ranks (attn: DP ranks, one per GPU since
+    # attn_tp_size == 1 is enforced; ffn: local TP ranks).
+    num_ranks: int
+    # Node identity for each instance rank, in rank order. NVSHMEM uses this
+    # to assign node-major PEs independently of the logical A/F rank space.
+    rank_node_ids: list[str] = field(repr=False)
+    afd_backend: str
+    # Logical F-internal expert layout. The attn process advertises the same
+    # layout after replacing its process-local backend with AFDAttnMoE.
+    afd_ffn_moe_backend: str
+    wire_dtype: str
+    moe_layers: list[dict] = field(repr=False)
+    direct_backend_version: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+    # F-authoritative per-layer activation quantization scales for native
+    # Direct NVFP4 dispatch. An empty list selects the FP8 activation path.
+    direct_nvfp4_input_scales: list[float] = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)
+    # F selects the FP8 scale encoding for every A/F rank, including empty inputs.
+    direct_deepep_fp8_scale_ue8m0: bool | None = None
+    # F owns the GEMM layout; every dispatcher must use matching expert offsets.
+    direct_deepep_expert_alignment: int = 128
+    # F-authoritative communication budget. Its meaning is data-plane specific;
+    # Direct DeepEP also uses it to size A-side Elastic kernels.
+    afd_comm_sm_budget: int | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+    # A-authoritative wire capacities. FULL uses global-token capacities;
+    # SCATTERED uses per-rank capacities.
+    decode_token_buckets: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)
+    # Stable first dimensions captured by this role's local decode graphs.
+    # Attn reports transport wire capacities; ffn reports expert capacities.
+    decode_graph_token_buckets: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)
+    disable_cuda_graph_padding: bool = False
+    # A-authoritative count used by the ffn side to allocate decode slots.
+    decode_num_microbatches: int = 1
+    # F-authoritative graph policy negotiated before A captures decode graphs.
+    requires_eager_decode_communication: bool = False
+    # Per-rank NVML fabric identity: (cluster UUID, clique ID). Missing or
+    # incomplete information conservatively requires a remote transport.
+    rank_nvshmem_fabric_keys: list[tuple[bytes, int] | None] = field(
+        default_factory=list, repr=False
+    )
+    # F-authoritative transport selected from the joint NVSHMEM topology.
+    nvshmem_remote_transport: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+    # A-authoritative fixed target-forward rows per request. Ordinary decode
+    # uses one; static EAGLE target verification uses its draft-token count.
+    decode_num_tokens_per_bs: int = 1
+    # F selects one transport mode for every rank and lane.
+    direct_deepep_allow_hybrid: bool = True
+

+class _HandshakeRequest(msgspec.Struct, tag="request", forbid_unknown_fields=True):
+    info: AFDHandshakeInfo
+    dist_host: str

+
+class _HandshakeReply(msgspec.Struct, tag="reply", forbid_unknown_fields=True):
+    info: AFDHandshakeInfo
+    dist_host: str
+    sync_port: int
+    dist_port: int
+    nvshmem_uid: bytes | None
+    session_id: int
+    attn_members: tuple[AFDHandshakeInfo, ...] | None
+
+
+class _HandshakeError(msgspec.Struct, tag="error", forbid_unknown_fields=True):
+    error: str

+_handshake_request_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(_HandshakeRequest)
+_handshake_reply_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(_HandshakeReply | _HandshakeError)

+@dataclass
+class AFDHandshakeResult:
+    local: AFDHandshakeInfo
+    peer: AFDHandshakeInfo
+    dist_host: str
+    sync_port: int
+    dist_port: int
+    nvshmem_uid: bytes | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+    # Index assigned by the ffn side in handshake-arrival order. Each attn
+    # instance forms its own session against a (possibly shared) ffn instance.
+    session_id: int = 0
+    # All attn instances sharing the ffn instance, in session order. Populated
+    # when the data plane forms one static world across every member.
+    attn_members: tuple[AFDHandshakeInfo, ...] | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+
+    @property
+    def requires_eager_decode_communication(self) -> bool:
+        ffn = self.local if self.local.role == "ffn" else self.peer
+        return ffn.requires_eager_decode_communication
+
+    @property
+    def total_attn_ranks(self) -> int:
+        if self.attn_members is None:
+            attn = self.local if self.local.role == "attn" else self.peer
+            return attn.num_ranks
+        return sum(member.num_ranks for member in self.attn_members)
+
+    @property
+    def attn_instance_rank_offset(self) -> int:
+        if self.attn_members is None:
+            return 0
+        if not 0 <= self.session_id < len(self.attn_members):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "AFD handshake session is outside the attn member roster: "
+                f"session={self.session_id}, members={len(self.attn_members)}"
+            )
+        return sum(member.num_ranks for member in self.attn_members[: self.session_id])
+
+
+def select_nvshmem_remote_transport(
+    ffn: AFDHandshakeInfo,
+    attn_members: tuple[AFDHandshakeInfo, ...],
+) -> str:
+    members = (ffn, *attn_members)
+    node_ids = {node_id for info in members for node_id in info.rank_node_ids}
+    if len(node_ids) <= 1:
+        return "none"
+
+    fabric_keys = [
+        fabric_key for info in members for fabric_key in info.rank_nvshmem_fabric_keys
+    ]
+    has_complete_fabric_topology = all(
+        len(info.rank_nvshmem_fabric_keys) == info.num_ranks for info in members
+    )
+    common_fabric_key = fabric_keys[0] if fabric_keys else None
+    if (
+        has_complete_fabric_topology
+        and common_fabric_key is not None
+        and any(common_fabric_key[0])
+        and all(fabric_key == common_fabric_key for fabric_key in fabric_keys)
+    ):
+        return "none"
+    return "ibgda"
+
